Let H,K be real complete Hilbert spaces and assume H is explicitly separable. Let D:H->partialLinear[R] K be a genuine real-linear partial operator on its actual submodule domain, with D.IsClosed (actual closed graph). Fix f:H. Let epsilon:N->R have epsilon_n>0 for every n and tend atTop to0 in R; monotonicity is not assumed. Let u:N->D.domain be a supplied actual solution family.
Assume for EVERY n and EVERY v:D.domain,
  epsilon_n*<u_n,v>_H+<D(u_n),D(v)>_K=<f,v>_H.
Assume for EVERY v:D.domain, D(v)=0 implies <f,v>_H=0. This is forcing orthogonality to every element of the actual kernel of this SAME partial operator.
Then BOTH limits hold simultaneously in genuine norm topologies:
  epsilon_n scalar-multiplied by (u_n as H) tends atTop to0 in H,
  epsilon_n scalar-multiplied by D(u_n) tends atTop to0 in K.
D is fixed before f,epsilon and solutions; this theorem applies to every supplied family satisfying all the actual variational equations. It does not construct another family. H and K need not be finite-dimensional; K separability, dense domain, bounded operator, supplied cluster/graph/limit certificate, or uniform unscaled-solution bound is not assumed. Ordinary product maxnorm is not silently identified with a Hilbert product. There is no abstract mean-zero replacement for all-kernel orthogonality and no assumption that solutions are centered. Both scalings are epsilon_n, not sqrt(epsilon_n). No rate, unscaled convergence, epsilon=0 solution, range/spectral-gap/further inequality or jointly measurable selection is concluded.

Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical ordinary volume, including dimension zero. Let W:E->R be C1 and assume exp(-W) volume-integrable. Define mu=volume.tilted(x->-W(x)), the actual normalized Gibbs probability exp(-W)/partition described in the approved full-space context. A separate positive-partition binder is not a displayed additional assumption.
For EVERY original real-linear partial operator D:Lp R 2 mu->partialLinear[R] Lp E 2 mu, assume D.IsClosable and exact original graph: for every scalar L2 a and vector L2 G, (a,G) is in D.graph iff there exists a smooth compactly supported real phi with a=phi mu-AE and G=gradient(phi) mu-AE. D.closure is the genuine same-graph closure operator on its actual submodule domain.
For EVERY actual scalar f:Lp R 2 mu satisfying integral f(x) dmu(x)=0, and EVERY epsilon:N->R with all epsilon_n>0 and Tendsto epsilon atTop0, both following conclusions hold:
(1) The actual standard representative x->f(x) is Integrable under mu.
(2) There exists ONE actual family u:N->D.closure.domain. For every n, this family satisfies ALL the following:
  for every v:D.closure.domain,
    epsilon_n*<u_n,v>_{L2(mu;R)}+<D.closure(u_n),D.closure(v)>_{L2(mu;E)}=<f,v>_{L2(mu;R)};
  the standard scalar representative of u_n and actual standard vector representative of D.closure(u_n) are each locally integrable with respect to ordinary volume;
  for every real C1 compactly supported psi and every direction a:E, BOTH x->psi(x)*<D.closure(u_n)(x),a>_E and x->u_n(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable, and
    integral psi(x)*<D.closure(u_n)(x),a>_E dx = - integral u_n(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
For this SAME family, epsilon_n scalar-multiplied by (u_n as scalar L2(mu)) tends atTop to the zero quotient strongly in genuine weighted L2 norm topology.
D precedes all centered forcing and all sequences. One family is selected after f/epsilon and before every n and every test. Forcing L1 and mean, all variational inner products and limit use actual mu; local integrability and ordinary weak-gradient products/integrals use volume. Actual L2 quotients and standard measurable representatives are retained. There is no monotonicity or centered-u assumption. Only scaled-function convergence is explicitly concluded here, not scaled-gradient convergence, C2 PDE/cutoff facts or an unscaled/range/epsilon=0/further inequality/core/main/cost composition theorem. There is no joint measurable selector.

Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical volume, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta:NNReal,eta:R. Assume alpha cast>0,alpha<=beta,V C2 and for every x,a:E BOTH
  alpha*||a||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a,
  (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a <= beta*||a||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define actual measures/potential
  mu=volume.tilted(x->-V(x)),
  J=map((x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g),mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta).
These are genuine normalized Gibbs tilt,independent product with standard real Hilbert Gaussian and pushforward.
There exist common kernels R,S:E->Measure E with R,S Markov,R a true conditional kernel for J.map Prod.swap,and for every y S(y)=(R(y)).map(x->2*x-y).
For EVERY y, S(y)=volume.tilted(z->-W_y(z)),W_y C2,exp(-W_y) volume-integrable with strictly positive volume integral. There exists ONE original real-linear partial gradient D:Lp R 2 (S(y))->partialLinear[R] Lp E 2 (S(y)) with dense domain in scalar L2,closability,closed closure,and exact graph: for every scalar a/vector G,(a,G) is in D.graph iff exists smooth compactly supported real phi with a=phi S(y)-AE and G=gradient(phi) S(y)-AE.
For EVERY actual scalar L2(S(y)) forcing f with integral f(x) dS(y)(x)=0,and EVERY epsilon:N->R positive at every n and tending atTop0,there exists ONE family u:N->this SAME D.closure.domain such that for EVERY n and EVERY v:D.closure.domain,
  epsilon_n*<u_n,v>_{L2(S(y);R)}+<D.closure(u_n),D.closure(v)>_{L2(S(y);E)}=<f,v>_{L2(S(y);R)},
and epsilon_n scalar-multiplied by the actual scalar L2(S(y)) class u_n tends atTop strongly to the zero quotient.
One common R,S precedes all y,one original D per y precedes ALL centered f and ALL positive-to-zero sequences,one family follows f/epsilon before every n and variational test. All y have density/operator facts;conditional disintegration has usual version scope,not a claim about all possible versions on every y. Only the literal reflected normalized-law equality is asserted,no equality of two distinct conditional kernels.
The displayed sequence output is exactly a variational family and scaled-function strong-zero. It does not separately list forcing Integrable,ordinary local weak/PDE/cutoff facts or scaled-gradient convergence as output conjuncts. Forcing is actual weighted L2 with actual law mean0;no abstract orthogonality premise or centered-u assumption replaces it. Partition integrability uses volume;means,inner products and limit use S(y). No monotonicity,rate,uniform unscaled bound,joint measurable y/f/sequence selection,unscaled/range/epsilon0/further functional inequality,score variance,full adjoint/core/Hessian or main/expected-cost composition conclusion is asserted.
